_source: The Chatterbox — Executive Weekly Health Report. Structure requested by Nick 2026-09-17; section list is his. Owners, cadence and the scorecard it aligns to (D01 CEO Enterprise Scorecard) come from TCB-KB-V3 modules 03/04/06.

_doctrine.deterministic: This file is a RULE BOOK, not a report. Every score in the report is computed by tools/build-exec-report.mjs from this file plus a week's data.json. No score is ever typed by hand or reasoned out by a model — same rule as the NBA engine (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 1).
_doctrine.absenceIsNotANought: A factor with no reading does not score 0. It leaves the denominator and the remaining factors in its section renormalise to 100, and the report says how much of the section was actually measured (`coverage`). The same doctrine as acComposite / perfScore (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 6). A factor that IS measured and is genuinely bad still scores low — an absence and a failure must never look the same.
_doctrine.basisIsPublished: Every value carries a basis: 'actual' (computed by AgentOS/PULSE from an uploaded source), 'manual' (a human-supplied number with a named owner), 'simulated' (a placeholder so the framework can be reviewed before the source exists) or 'absent'. Simulated values are badged on the face of the report and are EXCLUDED from the overall business score unless `countSimulated` is true. An executive must never be unable to tell a measured number from a placeholder (KB response contract, CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 8).
_doctrine.pointInTime: The report is a point-in-time view. It states its as-at date and the end date of every source feeding it, because the sources never end together (money, attendance, dialler and QA all cut on different days — specs/VAS-MTD-reconciliation.md).
_doctrine.oneNumberOneVerdict: A factor's score, band and RAG colour are derived once, here, and the page paints them. The HTML never re-derives a threshold (CLAUDE.md non-negotiable 12).
_doctrine.basisFollowsTheScore: A basis describes the SCORE, not just the value. A real reading measured against a placeholder target produces a placeholder score, so it is badged 'simulated' and the source line names the real figure inside it. September revenue is an actual number; 'revenue vs budget' is simulated until the CFO signs a budget.

_bandsNote: Deliberately NOT the agent bands in specs/composite_rules.json (Elite 90 / Strong 80 / On track 70 / Building 60 / Needs support). Those grade a person against a tenure target; these grade a department against plan, and the wording an executive acts on is different. Both sets are live-editable and neither may be copied into the other.
_coverageFloorNote: A section measured on less than half its weight is reported with its score AND a 'thin evidence' flag, and the score is shown as INDICATIVE — greyed, with the share actually measured beside it — because a figure standing on one factor out of eight is not the same kind of number as one standing on six. It still counts in the business score at its full weight. An earlier draft of this note promised the section would contribute 'at its measured coverage only'; that was never built, and on 2026-10-27 it was deliberately dropped rather than implemented — see _changes.
_countSimulatedNote: TRUE for this first framework build only, so every section produces a number and the shape can be reviewed. Set FALSE once real feeds land and the overall score must be defensible — the generator then scores only 'actual' and 'manual' readings and reports the rest as coverage gaps.

scales._note: How a raw reading becomes 0-100. Every factor names one. 'target' = value ÷ target, capped; 'targetDown' = target ÷ value, capped (lower is better); 'band' = step bands, first match wins, listed high to low; 'pct' = the value already IS a 0-100 score.
scales._capNote: Over-achievement is capped at 110 before weighting, so one runaway factor cannot mask a failing one. Capped at 110 rather than 100 so genuine over-delivery still shows.

_changes.to: a thin section is shown as indicative and still counts at full weight
_changes.why: Measured on real data only, LRC scores 0 on one factor of eight — zero of thirteen registered systems at G4. Weighting that section down by its 10% coverage would have lifted the business score from 74.3 to about 86 and quietly buried the single worst measured number in the report. A thin section is a reason to distrust the FIGURE, never a reason to discount the FINDING. The flag and the greying say so; the arithmetic does not move.

_bandScaleNote: A count whose target is ZERO cannot be scored as value ÷ target — one incident would read 0 and two would read 0, and the report could not tell a wobble from a crisis. Those factors carry step BANDS in this file instead, first match wins, listed high to low: the rule book says what one critical fail is worth and what eight are worth, and the generator only looks it up.

viz._note: Presentation parameters for the report, validated rather than eyeballed. Campaign hues are an IDENTITY channel (a dot beside the name); the bars themselves are one hue, because their job is magnitude — colouring a bar by its own length double-encodes it. Status colours mean state and are never used for a series.
viz._validated: node scripts/validate_palette.js "#2563EB,#0E8C74,#C2410C,#7C4DE0,#BE1D74" --mode light --surface "#FFFFFF" — 5/5 checks pass (lightness band, chroma floor, CVD separation, normal-vision floor, contrast). The VAS dark-theme campaign hues (#4C9DFF/#2BD9B0/#A78BFA) FAIL on a white surface: too light, and every slot under 3:1. These are their light-surface steps, same hue families.
viz._statusNote: Status fills are the darker text-safe steps (all ≥3:1 on white) and the track is the lighter step of the same ramp, so the state reads across the whole bar. A status colour never carries meaning alone on this page — every bar is labelled with its band.

_feedNote: Every factor names the FEED behind it — the system, the store, the exact fields, the grain, the cadence and the owner — plus a PROBE the coverage tool runs against this repo. The probe decides the state; the rule book never declares one. `node tools/exec-coverage.mjs` is the test, and reports/exec-weekly/DATA-REQUIREMENTS.md is its output.
_stateNote: The coverage tool derives FIVE states, and `partial` is the one that matters most: a probe can find the value and still not find what the value is MEASURED AGAINST. Revenue is exact to the rand and 'revenue vs budget' is unscoreable, because no budget exists. Counting those as 'exists, not wired' would have flattered the plan by about a sixth of the business score.
